hero.title: Welcome in Rio, <1>hope</1> in Congo
hero.subtitle: Since 2010, Casa Esperança Real Crescer has been welcoming refugees and vulnerable families in Rio de Janeiro and bringing food, shelter and hope to the Indigenous pygmy peoples of Congo.

about.title: A mission born from welcoming others
about.p1: It all began with Pastor Leonardo (Laza Ndosi), a missionary since 1998, who arrived in Brazil in 2003. In Rio de Janeiro, he found African communities in Brás de Pina, Caxias, Gramacho and downtown. He then began helping refugees as an interpreter at Caritas and the Federal Police, where he also taught Portuguese for several years.
about.p2: In 2010, with the help of his friend Pastor Marcos Fernandes, Casa Esperança Real Crescer was born: an NGO dedicated to helping people in need in local communities, welcoming foreigners who arrive without family, and supporting the villages of Indigenous pygmy peoples in Africa.
about.p3: Distribution of food baskets, free haircut and braiding days, mental health support and free dental care are some of the actions we carry out to this day.
about.image_alt: Community gathered under a thatched shelter in a village

projects.title: What we do
projects.subtitle: From Rio de Janeiro to the villages of Congo, our projects bring dignity, food and hope.

congo.title: Mission with Indigenous pygmy peoples
congo.description: Supporting the villages of Indigenous pygmy peoples in Congo with food, building materials and assistance to families.

housing.title: Decent housing
housing.description: Delivering roofing sheets and building materials so families can rebuild their homes safely.

refugees.title: Welcoming refugees
refugees.description: Shelter, interpretation, Portuguese lessons and guidance for foreigners arriving in Brazil without family.

community.title: Community social work
community.description: Food basket distribution, free haircuts and braiding, mental health support and dental care in Brás de Pina.

founder.title: Pastor Leonardo
founder.quote: With the help of God, kind-hearted people, companies and public institutions, we will continue our mission.
founder.p1: Laza Ndosi, known as Pastor Leonardo, has been a missionary since 1998, devoting his life to God's work and to social action. In 2009 he founded Betesda International, a church that welcomes foreigners and teaches the word of God.
founder.p2: To this day we continue to welcome people, guide them and do social work, with many ongoing projects in Brazil and Africa.
